what_this_is: Two runs of the SAME harness, config and seed, so every per-task delta is pure run-to-run variation. This is what metric_noise.py structurally cannot see: it bootstraps by resampling the model side of a FIXED set of rows, capturing sampling noise but not generation variation between runs. vLLM with continuous batching at max_parallel_participants=50 is not reproducible at temperature 0, because batch composition changes reduction order.
headline: The enforced floors are CONSERVATIVE, not too tight. The largest run-to-run movement across the eight search tasks is 0.0152, on digit_span_forward, whose floor is 0.140. The 8-task mean moves +0.0001 against a min credible mean delta of 0.026.
headline_amended: PARTLY REVISED by a second measurement, see second_measurement below. One repeat of the BASELINE was not enough: a harness that overflows is noisier than one that refuses, and narrative_qa reaches 0.0160 rather than the 0.0065 measured here -- over half its 0.030 floor. The floors are still all above the measured noise, but narrative's margin is thin and no narrative effect below about 0.02 should be claimed.

second_measurement.what: primacy (iter2) and primacy_v2 (iter3) were the SAME harness, discovered after the fact, which makes the pair a second run-to-run measurement -- and a better one than the repeat baseline, because this harness OVERFLOWS and the baseline does not.
why_identical: primacy_v2's batch rule never fired: craft's overflowing rows settled at occupancy 4.0, primacy's value.
For a SINGLE eviction primacy_v2's tool-result string is byte-identical to primacy's; the plural form exists only for a double eviction, which therefore never occurred.

Replaying the real write sequences from both live runs through both memory classes under serial arrival: ZERO divergences over 874 rows and 3610 write calls, comparing store contents and returned strings at every call.

A3_precision_distance.note: the sharpest illustration: 'closest to the human median any candidate reached' described nothing at all

consequences: narrative_qa's noise is up to 0.0160, not 0.0065. primacy's -0.0309 violation is about twice the observed spread rather than five times it -- still probably real, but the margin is much thinner than previously stated.
craft_task's near-exactness is confirmed by a second, independent pair: 0.0031 here against 0.0000 from the repeat baseline. So craft remains the most trustworthy gist cell.
The 8-task mean is stable to 0.0001 across BOTH measurements, so the 0.026 min credible mean delta holds.
METHODOLOGICAL: one measurement of run-to-run variation does not license reading a delta. Noise must be measured on a harness of the same family as the candidate, not on the baseline.

findings: Generation variation does NOT propagate to the score uniformly, and that is the durable lesson. semantic_story_recall has 156 of 200 rows differing for a delta of -0.0012, because the score is a continuous embedding similarity and the variation averages out. craft_task and word_recognition have ZERO rows differing, because a coarse multiple-choice score cannot register a rewording. narrative_qa is the sensitive cell: 13 of 50 rows differ for -0.0065, the largest scored effect per differing row in the set.

narrative_qa's real run-to-run noise is 0.0065, not the 0.030 its floor asserts. So primacy's -0.0309 is about five times the measured noise and is a genuine effect. It violates the floor by only 0.0009 because 0.030 is conservative, not because the effect is marginal. The earlier reading -- that a 0.0009 violation is unsupportable by the instrument -- was half right: the violation is real, the threshold is the arbitrary part.

craft_task is fully reproducible at the score level, 0 of 150 rows and delta exactly 0.0000. So primacy's -0.0451 and episodic_reset's -0.0280 on this task are both real effects, and iteration 3a's second-order claim that craft's floor understates run-to-run variation is refuted.

digit_span_forward's +0.0152 is the largest run-to-run movement measured, and it is EXACTLY the value primacy reported for that task (chunk_limit reported +0.0183). Those digit-span moves were run-to-run variation, not mechanism -- which confirms primacy's P4 no-change claim, for the right reason rather than the one it gave.
The 8-task mean is stable to +0.0001, so the 0.026 min credible mean delta is amply conservative and a mean movement above it remains meaningful.
consequences_for_the_contract: No floor needs loosening. All eight enforced floors exceed the measured run-to-run variation, most by a wide margin.

A no-change prediction may NOT demand bit-identity of generated content -- content varies on every task. It MAY reasonably demand a scored delta under about 0.007 on craft_task, word_recognition, digit_span_reverse, semantic_story_recall, nback and variable_mapping, and under about 0.016 on digit_span_forward.

A differing-row count remains a far more sensitive mechanism-confirmation quantity than a scored delta, but it must be compared against this table's row counts rather than against zero: 156 of 200 differing rows on story recall is the NO-CHANGE baseline there, not evidence of anything.

third_measurement_episodic_family.what: Two runs of IDENTICAL code for respond_first and respond_only (jobs 18684882/18715439 and 18717242). On craft_task these candidates are provable no-ops -- the request sequences driven through the real encode path are byte-identical to the baseline's, same message counts, roles, tool_choice and final store -- so any spread is pure run-to-run variation.
third_measurement_episodic_family.why_it_matters: The 0.030 enforced floor sits INSIDE the noise for craft_task and narrative_qa on this harness family, so single-run accept/reject verdicts on those two tasks are coin flips. Both candidates pass in one run and fail in the other, on DIFFERENT tasks.

craft_task.note: In both B runs craft lands on EXACTLY the baseline value. craft is bimodal here: either identical to baseline or about -0.035.

narrative_qa.note: respond_first run B fails the narrative floor at -0.0314 where run A passes it.

consequences: The MEAN is reliable and the per-task floors are not, at the magnitude these mechanisms operate at: mean spread 0.002-0.006 against per-task spreads of 0.029-0.037 on craft and narrative.
Earlier rejections on those two tasks are suspect: primacy's narrative -0.0309, chunk_limit's narrative -0.0310, and every craft violation in iterations 5 and 6.
Acceptance needs either multiple runs per candidate with a proper test, or floors set from SAME-FAMILY repeats rather than from the baseline. An arm is 14 minutes, so both are affordable.
Third instance of the same error: craft's noise rested on two observations from other harness families, exactly as narrative's did before it went 0.0065 to 0.0160 when a second pair arrived.
